title: Jonathan Kuminga Signs Two-Year, $13 Million Deal With Minnesota Timberwolves
dek: Jonathan Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $13 million contract with the Minnesota Timberwolves as an unrestricted free agent, using the taxpayer mid-level exception. The signing bolsters Minnesota's wing depth alongside Anthony Edwards and Rudy Gobert. Kuminga's free agency lingered into late summer for the second consecutive year.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Kuminga signed a two-year, $13 million deal with Minnesota, a below-market settlement after extended free agency.
bottom_line: Kuminga's $13 million settlement after two consecutive slow free agencies reflects either declining market confidence or his own strategic choices. How Minnesota's ball movement and defense evolve with a roster this substantially rebuilt will frame whether Kuminga's late addition proves a fit or a sign of incomplete team construction.
body:
Jonathan Kuminga signed a two-year, $13 million contract with the Minnesota Timberwolves using the taxpayer mid-level exception, according to Yahoo Sports. The signing settles the forward's free agency after a summer-long wait that marked the second consecutive offseason in which Kuminga lingered on the market.
Anthony Edwards helped recruit Kuminga, who accepted less money per year in exchange for a shorter deal, according to Yahoo Sports. The Timberwolves will likely need to trade Donte DiVincenzo or Josh Green, or waive-and-stretch Green, to create the necessary cap space below the second apron, per the reporting.
Kuminga's path to Minnesota began with his selection by the Golden State Warriors with the seventh overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft. The Warriors traded him to the Atlanta Hawks for Kristaps Porzingis before the trade deadline. In 16 regular-season games with Atlanta at 22.1 minutes per game, Kuminga averaged 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists on 47.6 percent from the field, 34.6 percent from three, and 70.2 percent from the free throw line, per Yahoo Sports. The Hawks declined his team option, allowing him to enter free agency.
A year prior, as a restricted free agent, Phoenix and Sacramento each offered Kuminga more than $60 million in guarantees, according to Yahoo Sports. He declined both offers and re-signed with Golden State on a one-year, $23.8 million deal with a team option. That choice preceded this summer's quieter market reception and shorter contract term.
Minnesota remade its roster by trading Naz Reid and Julius Randle and replacing them with Ball and Kuminga, per Yahoo Sports reporting. Yahoo Sports describes the configuration as one of the Western Conference's highest-risk, highest-reward teams, with Kuminga positioned as an unproven piece on a roster centered around an injury-prone All-Star.
